notes: acServer has no RCON, no interactive console and no admin HTTP API, so there is no command text a server manager can send. Evidence: the Pelican/Pterodactyl egg stops it with SIGINT (^C) rather than a console command; third-party panels (ac-server-interface) drive it purely by editing cfg/server_cfg.ini and managing the process; guides describe ADMIN_PASSWORD only as the credential 'used in chat as /admin <pass>'. Moderation exists, but only down two channels this schema cannot express. (1) In-game chat: a connected client that authenticates with /admin <password> can then type /kick, /ban, /kick_id <car_id>, /ban_id <car_id>, /client_list, /next_session, /restart_session - these are typed by a player in the game client, not by the host. (2) The binary UDP plugin protocol configured by UDP_PLUGIN_ADDRESS / UDP_PLUGIN_LOCAL_PORT in server_cfg.ini, which carries KICK_USER, BROADCAST_CHAT and SEND_CHAT; it is not text, must be configured before the server starts, and accepts only one plugin (ACSRelay exists to multiplex that single slot). HTTP_PORT (default 8081) serves read-only lobby/entry-list JSON (/INFO, /JSON) for Content Manager and the lobby, not admin actions. Bans land as one SteamID64 per line in blacklist.txt in the server root, read into memory at startup, so deleting a line needs a server restart. Disagreement: the Assetto Corsa Server Manager documentation (mirrored by Emperor Servers and Chiphead) lists /unban <GUID>, /ban_list and /guid_list as chat commands, which hosting docs and older command lists do not mention; those may be Server Manager or Custom Shaders Patch additions rather than vanilla acServer, and were not confirmed. XGamingServer's page additionally claims a server-side console accepting bare 'kick'/'ban'/'clients'/'quit'; no other source supports that and it is treated as wrong.
